title: License and permitted use
description: Apache License 2.0 permits commercial use, modifications, distribution, and paid hosting.
body:
## Apache License 2.0

Skiva uses the standard **Apache License 2.0** (SPDX: Apache-2.0). Individuals and companies may self-host, modify, distribute, sell, and offer paid hosting. Skiva adds no prohibition on commercial use or profitable derivatives.

## Distribution requirements

Provide the license text to recipients, clearly identify modified files, retain applicable copyright and attribution notices, and preserve applicable NOTICE contents as required by section 4. The license does not require disclosure of all modified source code.

The license includes a patent grant and termination conditions. It does not automatically grant trademark rights. Warranty exclusions and liability limitations are governed by the license text.

## Third-party and user content

Third-party components retain their own licenses. Your Skills, business data, and Agent output do not automatically inherit Skiva's license merely because you use the platform.

## Authoritative files

[LICENSE](https://github.com/LingHeChen/skiva/blob/main/LICENSE) · [NOTICE](https://github.com/LingHeChen/skiva/blob/main/NOTICE) · [License FAQ](https://github.com/LingHeChen/skiva/blob/main/LICENSE-FAQ.md) · [Third-party notices](https://github.com/LingHeChen/skiva/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)

The LICENSE accompanying your version governs use. This explanation adds no restrictions. See the official [Apache License 2.0](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0).

title: Using the repository workspace
description: Browse Git files, diagnose validation failures, and review complete release sets.
body:
## Find your way around

Open a repository in [Git repositories](/repositories) and switch between Overview, Files, Skills, Pipelines, and Settings. Use ⌘ K / Ctrl K to search for a repository or page, then press Enter.

## Files and source

Hosted repositories support Git ref selection, file search, expandable directories, Markdown previews, and numbered source views. Files are pinned to the current tree's commit SHA. Commit history lets you browse a historical tree.

Text previews are limited to 256 KiB. Download binary files using Git. External repositories show built Skill versions; browse original files at the source Git service. Expand the metadata section in Markdown previews to inspect frontmatter.

## Maintain repositories

Settings provides Git Tokens, membership, branch protection, commits, diffs, and synchronization. Edit configuration to change scan scope. Commit `.skills-platform.yaml` to define repository validation; see [Pipeline configuration](/docs/pipelines).

## Prepare a release

Prepare release opens an organization-wide drawer. It inherits the complete Stable set, even when opened from one repository. Combine Skills from multiple repositories, replace versions, inspect before/after file differences, and review every removal.

The server must validate the complete preview before you can create an immutable snapshot. Changing selected versions or risk acknowledgement invalidates the previous preview. Creating a snapshot does not promote a channel.

## Snapshots and channels

Snapshot details include Full content, Version differences, and Channels and history. The current snapshot is preselected as a target in Channels and history. Enter a reason and confirm to promote it. Use a historical snapshot for rollback. Server permissions, generation checks, and idempotency keys protect these operations.

## Diagnostics and Agents

Pipeline details show server validation diagnostics by stage. Search messages, paths, or rule IDs and filter errors. This panel does not run an arbitrary shell.

Mount clients shows the last reported snapshot alongside the channel target. Pinned tasks do not follow channel updates automatically. Organization permissions, security, and account settings remain available in the sidebar.

title: From Skill commits to Agent delivery
description: Publish, update, and roll back your team's Skills with a verifiable delivery process.
body:
## One complete delivery path

Git supplies content. Skiva validates fixed commits, stores immutable versions, and delivers complete snapshots through channels.

**Git commit → Pipeline validation → Skill version → Release snapshot → Canary verification → Stable → Agent**

A successful build does not publish content. Creating a snapshot does not change a channel. Clients following a channel discover a new version only after that channel is promoted.

## Where to start

| Goal | Guide |
| --- | --- |
| Create a Git repository in Skiva | [Hosted Git](/docs/managed-git) |
| Use the platform for the first time | [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart) |
| Understand versions, snapshots, and channels | [Core concepts](/docs/concepts) |
| Publish, update, or roll back Skills | [Releases](/docs/releases) |
| Configure scan directories and rules | [Pipelines](/docs/pipelines) |
| Connect an Agent | [Clients and Agents](/docs/clients) |
| Manage permissions and credentials | [Security](/docs/security) |
| Deploy, back up, or troubleshoot | [Operations](/docs/operations) |

## Supported scope

The console, static Git validation, immutable releases, Canary / Stable channels, Profile authorization, and Linux read-only FUSE mounts are implemented. Pipelines do not execute repository scripts. Native macOS / Windows mounts are not implemented.

> This handbook describes the current implementation. Agent context caches and filesystem updates are separate: after files change, you may still need to reload Skills or start a new task.

## Python SDK

Connect your own Agent with versioned discovery, pinned/dynamic views and Pydantic AI integration. Start with the [Python SDK quickstart](/docs/sdk-python).

title: Make your first release
description: Follow a repository through validation, publication, and authorized delivery.
body:
## Before you begin

Sign in to the [console](/dashboard). Administrator credentials come from your deployment configuration. See [Operations](/docs/operations) to start a local instance.

If enterprise-demo exists, use its sql-query and code-review Skills. Otherwise, connect your own repository below.

## 1. Connect and synchronize a repository

In [Git repositories](/repositories), add the remote URL, credential reference, default ref (for example, refs/heads/main), and Skill root `skills`. Private Git hosts must satisfy the deployment's allowlist and network policy.

Test the connection, then synchronize. Inspect [Pipelines](/pipelines). For failures, fix the reported files, rules, or lines, commit, and synchronize again.

## 2. Inspect candidate versions

In [Skills Registry](/skills), verify the name, description, source commit, and file tree. Open SKILL.md and check referenced files.

Successful validation prepares a candidate; it does not change a live channel.

## 3. Create a complete snapshot

Open [Create release](/releases/new). Review the set inherited from Stable, add Skills, and replace versions that need updating. Preview the complete view, review warnings and affected Profiles, then create the immutable snapshot.

> A snapshot is a complete set, not a patch. If production contains A, B, and C, updating A still requires A's new version and the existing B and C versions. The drawer inherits Stable by default and explicitly reports removals.

## 4. Promote Canary first

In [Release channels](/channels), select the new snapshot for Canary, review differences, enter a reason, and confirm. Record the snapshot ID. After verification, promote that same snapshot to Stable.

## 5. Connect a test Agent

Create a test [Agent Profile](/profiles): channel canary, explicitly authorized Skills, and dynamic mode. Register a [mount client](/clients) for it and save the token, which is shown only once.

Follow the [client guide](/docs/clients) to mount on Linux and connect an Agent. Verify both file contents and Agent behavior before promoting Stable.

## Completion checklist

- The pipeline succeeds and Registry shows the expected commit.
- Canary points to the new snapshot; Stable stays unchanged until promotion.
- The test client reads only Skills authorized by its Profile.
- After Stable promotion, new opens on dynamic clients see updated content.
- The release appears in the [audit log](/audit).

title: Host Git repositories in Skiva
description: Create repositories, control pushes, and reuse the existing release workflow.
body:
## Create a repository and push

Choose Hosted in Git repositories → New. Enter namespace, slug, and display name; choose a single-Skill, monorepo, or empty template. Creation returns provisioning; the worker changes it to active when ready and retains errors for retry on failure.

A namespace belongs to one organization. namespace/slug is unique within it and stays reserved after soft deletion. Physical storage uses an immutable UUID. Display name and API namespace/slug can change without moving storage; old clone URLs return 404 rather than redirecting reads or writes. Update your remote. External repositories are not automatically converted to hosted ones.

Create a repository Git Token. Read-only tokens allow clone/fetch; enable repo:write for pushes. Maximum lifetime is 90 days. Plaintext is shown once: store it in your OS credential manager, never in repositories, URLs, or logs. Git tokens differ from mount credentials.

```bash
git clone https://skills.example.internal/git/engineering/sql-query.git
cd sql-query
# Supply the Git Token when Git requests a password
# Edit SKILL.md and referenced files
git add .
git commit -m 'Improve instructions'
git push origin main
```

The first push to an empty repository must include SKILL.md. Monorepos default to skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md. Standard Git HTTPS is supported; SSH, LFS, pull requests, and issues are not.

## Push, build, and release are separate

A successful push means Git accepted the update. Activity records the actual ref and SHA; the worker hands a fixed commit to the existing pipeline. The default branch and refs/tags/v* build automatically by default. Other branches only record activity.

A successful pipeline creates candidate Skill versions. Follow [Releases](/docs/releases) to create a complete snapshot, validate Canary, and promote Stable with release permission. Push and repository maintenance permissions do not grant release permission. Existing delivery clients and tokens remain compatible.

Inspect Push → Pipeline, Commits, Branches / Tags, Files, and Diff. Clicking a commit SHA shows fixed-version files. Diff display/download is capped at 256 KiB with explicit truncation; use local git diff for the full result. Filenames and differences are rendered as text, not executable HTML.

## Membership and protection

| Repository role | Read | Push unprotected branches | Protected main | Configure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Viewer | Yes | No | No | No |
| Contributor | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| Maintainer / Org Admin | Yes | Yes | Per policy | Yes |

The organization-level repo_maintainer role does not grant all hosted repositories. Creators become repository Maintainers; only Org Admin can administer across repositories. Add same-organization members by user UUID. Database constraints reject cross-organization grants.

Tokens are scoped to one repository. Every request checks expiry, scope, current user state, and current membership. Permission changes and revocation affect new requests immediately; an existing transfer may run until its 120-second timeout. Rotate by creating a token, updating and verifying the client, then revoking the old token.

By default, main blocks force pushes and deletion. Only Maintainers can create protected tags; overwriting/deleting them is forbidden. pre-receive rejects the entire invalid batch and supports git push --atomic. Limits cover file count, object size, push size, repository size, and global capacity. Symlinks, submodules, dangerous binaries, and sensitive paths are forbidden. scripts/ can be stored but never executed by the server. CI independently checks content, references, and secrets.

Defaults: 64 MiB per push, 512 MiB per repository, 4 MiB per object, 10,000 files, 1,000 repositories per organization, 20 GiB global hosted storage. Git response buffering is capped at 32 MiB. Oversized clones return a gateway error; changes require capacity and load qualification, not an assumption of unlimited storage.

## Operations and rollback

Apply additive migration 00003 first. Existing rows become external; historical SHAs, versions, and snapshots remain unchanged. All three flags default to false:

```bash
SKIVA_MANAGED_GIT_ENABLED=true
SKIVA_MANAGED_GIT_WRITE_ENABLED=true
SKIVA_MANAGED_GIT_AUTO_CI_ENABLED=true
SKIVA_GIT_PUBLIC_URL=https://skills.example.internal
```

Enable creation/reads, then writes, then automatic CI. Production requires HTTPS. Set SKIVA_GIT_TRUST_PROXY=true only behind a trusted proxy that overwrites X-Forwarded-Proto and prevents direct backend access. Route /git/ directly to Go, not the Next.js BFF. See deployments/nginx-git.conf.

Local development can explicitly enable SKIVA_GIT_ALLOW_LOOPBACK_HTTP=true; production ignores it. The public URL is display configuration, not a request-supplied disk path.

Disabling WRITE_ENABLED rejects new pushes. Disabling AUTO_CI_ENABLED pauses event enqueueing. Disabling ENABLED hides the capability and stops Git ingress. Retain database columns, bare repositories, and events; re-enable after repair. Already-queued jobs continue on fixed SHAs and published distribution content remains readable. Do not run destructive down migrations.

Sources live at SKIVA_DATA_DIR/managed-git/<storage-id>.git; durable events at git-spool/. Back up both with PostgreSQL, objects/, and configuration/Secret references. Stop writes and workers before scripts/backup.sh. Restore into a new database/directory with scripts/restore.sh, which checks CAS and git fsck. Then verify fetch/push, rebuild, snapshots, and authorized client reads. File counts alone do not prove recovery. Soft-deleted repository storage remains by default without automatic GC.

post-receive atomically writes events; it does not run CI. The worker imports events into the database/queue and reconciles refs/reflogs. Do not delete reflogs or run destructive Git GC. Provisioning/failed metadata is also reconciled and retried.

## Troubleshooting

- 401: check Git PAT expiry/revocation and remove stale credential-manager passwords.
- 404: incorrect path, missing permission, or absent repository; the API intentionally does not distinguish them.
- 403: HTTPS required, writes disabled, or repository disabled.
- Rejected push: inspect main/tag protection, force push, deletion, file types, and quotas. Git displays the server reason.
- Push succeeds without a build: check automatic CI, trigger refs, activity errors, and queue backlog. Some refs only record activity.
- 502: process failure, 120-second timeout, or output limit. Fetch to verify remote state before retrying a push.
- 507: disk/global quota exhausted. Preserve published reads, expand capacity, then resume pushes.
- Provisioning failure: inspect volume permissions, disk, and the Git executable. The worker retries after repair; do not delete logical IDs to bypass errors.

Monitor git_http_requests_total, git_receive_bytes_total, git_push_rejected_total, git_ref_event_pending, git_ref_reconcile_lag_seconds, git_process_duration_seconds_*, and managed_repository_provision_failures_total under /metrics. Run make verify-artifacts during quiet periods for CAS and git fsck.

Actual enterprise IdP, target TLS proxy, Linux FUSE + Agent sandbox, capacity, and disk/power-loss drills remain deployment gates. Developer-machine and CI results do not certify production acceptance.

title: Versions, snapshots, and delivery
description: Understand the six objects that determine who receives an update.
body:
## Six core objects

| Object | Responsibility | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Repository | Git source and synchronization configuration | Team Skills repository |
| Skill Version | Immutable content of one Skill | Updated sql-query instructions |
| Release Snapshot | Complete set of Skill versions | New A + existing B + existing C |
| Channel | Mutable pointer to a snapshot | canary, stable |
| Agent Profile | Channel, allowed Skills, mode, offline policy | Engineering test assistant |
| Mount Client | Independent endpoint identity and credentials | An Agent on a build machine |

## Why snapshots exist

An Agent can use multiple Skills. A snapshot fixes their version combination for reproducibility and whole-set rollback. Identical sets can be deduplicated; snapshot content cannot be edited after creation.

To update, create a snapshot and change the channel pointer. Old snapshots remain readable without the Git remote being online.

## Profiles control visibility

A channel supplies a version set. A Profile authorizes selected Skills from it. Clients can read only authorized files; selecting a Skill absent from the channel snapshot does not make it appear.

A useful starting point is a test Profile following canary and a production Profile following stable. They may authorize different Skills.

## Dynamic and pinned modes

| Mode | Update behavior | Suitable use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dynamic | Refreshes the index after channel updates; new opens use the new version | Long-running interactive assistants |
| pinned | Retains its bound snapshot until explicit repin | Tasks requiring stable versions |

Existing open handles retain old content. Dynamic mode does not guarantee the same snapshot across multiple opens within one long task; use pinned for that requirement.

## Channel generation

Every successful promotion or rollback increments generation. This prevents two administrators from overwriting each other's release. On a conflict, refresh and review current differences before retrying.

title: Publish, update, and roll back
description: Verify content on Canary, then deliver the same snapshot to production.
body:
## Prepare Skill content

A repository can contain multiple Skills:

```text
repository/
├── .skills-platform.yaml
└── skills/
    ├── sql-query/
    │   ├── SKILL.md
    │   └── references/guide.md
    └── code-review/
        └── SKILL.md
```

Example SKILL.md:

```markdown
---
name: sql-query
description: Analyze database schemas and write read-only queries.
---

Read the [query guidelines](references/guide.md) before querying.
```

Commit SKILL.md together with referenced files. Skiva does not follow symbolic links or recursively fetch submodules.

## Update an existing Skill

1. Change content in Git, commit, and push to the configured ref.
2. A webhook triggers synchronization; you can also synchronize manually. The worker checks periodically every minute.
3. Inspect pipeline diagnostics, the Registry version, and file differences.
4. Create a complete snapshot with the updated Skill and unchanged versions of other Skills.
5. Promote Canary and verify test-client files and Agent behavior.
6. Promote the same snapshot to Stable and record the reason.

> Configuration or validator changes may revalidate the same commit. Unchanged content does not necessarily create a new content version.

## Review before publishing

- Did the complete set accidentally omit another Skill?
- Are all relative references present?
- Have security warnings been reviewed? Blockers must be fixed; acknowledgement cannot bypass them.
- Are affected Profiles expected?
- Do pinned clients need a repin between tasks?

## Roll back a channel

Choose a snapshot previously used by that channel, enter a reason, and confirm. Rollback creates a new history record and generation; it does not rebuild Git.

Dynamic clients follow the rolled-back channel. Pinned clients retain their snapshot until explicitly repinned between tasks. Content already loaded into an Agent's context does not disappear automatically.

## Confirm delivery

Check the client's latest heartbeat and snapshot ID in the console or run status. Use refresh for an explicit refresh. SSE provides hints and polling is the fallback; instantaneous switching of every endpoint is not guaranteed.

```bash
skills-mount status
skills-mount refresh
# Pinned: run only between tasks
skills-mount refresh --repin
```

If you use a custom `--cache`, pass the same cache path to these commands.

title: Configure validation pipelines
description: Control scan scope and static policies without executing repository code.
body:
## What pipelines do

Stages are fixed: safely fetch Git, discover SKILL.md, statically validate, and store content and versions. Builds bind to a fixed commit SHA. Webhooks, manual synchronization, and periodic checks use the same job queue.

Arbitrary step orchestration, shell execution, and custom test plugins are not supported. Repository scripts may be inspected but are never executed by the pipeline.

## Repository configuration

Commit `.skills-platform.yaml` at the repository root:

```yaml
version: 1

skills:
  root: skills

pipeline:
  trigger:
    branches:
      - main

validate:
  blockScripts: true
  blockExternalLinks: true
```

| Setting | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| version | Only 1 is accepted |
| skills.root | Scan directory; overrides the repository page's root |
| pipeline.trigger.branches | Validates the configured branch against an allowlist |
| pipeline.trigger.tags | Validates tags when the default ref targets a tag |
| validate.blockScripts | Blocks detected script content |
| validate.blockExternalLinks | Blocks detected external links |

Branches and tags use exact matching, such as main or refs/heads/main. Wildcards such as release/* are not supported here. Multiple entries do not create multiple branch listeners: the repository's default ref remains the synchronization target. A mismatch produces a configuration diagnostic. Omitting a list adds no restriction for that ref type.

Unknown fields are rejected. Adding steps or run does not enable command execution.

## Organization policy

[Security settings](/settings/security) controls per-file bytes, total bytes, file count, scripts, and external links. Defaults are 8 MiB per file, 64 MiB total, and 10,000 files. Tree resource limits can cover files throughout the fetched tree; keep repositories focused.

Repository configuration can tighten but cannot relax organization policy. Setting false cannot disable an organization-level block. Static detection does not prove content safe; publishers must still review warnings.

## Webhooks and reconciliation

Repository details provides webhook URLs and configuration. GitHub, GitLab, and Gitea use provider signatures or shared tokens and delivery-ID deduplication.

The worker checks remotes every minute to recover missed webhooks. Builds deduplicate unchanged commits and effective configurations. Expired Git credentials affect future synchronization, not existing published snapshots.

## Custom tests and model evaluations

Run custom tests in external CI. Merge approved commits into the tracked branch, then let Skiva validate and deliver them.

```text
Feature branch → External CI tests / evaluations → Merge main
               → Skiva sync and validation → Canary → Stable
```

Skiva does not enforce an external-CI release gate. Configure required checks and branch protection at the Git service if passing evaluations must be mandatory.

## Read diagnostics

Diagnostics include ruleId, severity, file path, line, and explanation. Fix blockers and commit again; review warnings before release. Fetch failures may appear only as synchronization errors because no buildable commit has been resolved yet.

Discovery, validation, and content writes share one static scan. Displayed stage times may overlap and must not be summed as total duration.

title: Connect clients and Agents
description: Mount authorized Skills and control version updates and offline behavior.
body:
## SDK or filesystem mount

For a custom Python Agent, start with the [Python SDK](/docs/sdk-python): no FUSE required, with snapshot-versioned discovery. For an existing Agent that only accepts directories, use the Linux mount below. Cache, offline and context-update semantics differ; see [integration choices](/docs/sdk-files). Mode and offline-policy descriptions below apply to mount clients. The SDK defaults to pinned views with online validation; dynamic behavior is opt-in.

## Create a Profile and client identity

Choose a Profile's channel, Skills, dynamic or pinned mode, and offline policy. Ensure the channel has a snapshot. Register a mount client and save its one-time token. If lost, rotate it; the platform does not reveal the original again.

Use separate credentials per endpoint. The server Profile determines the mode; a client cannot change channels or expand its own access.

## Mount on Linux

You need Linux FUSE, an accessible /dev/fuse, and mount permissions. Place the matching architecture's skills-mount executable on PATH. Native macOS / Windows mounting is not implemented.

For a dynamic Profile, replace the server and PROFILE_ID below and save the token to client.token:

```bash
chmod 600 client.token
skills-mount login \
  --server https://skills.example.internal \
  --token-file client.token

skills-mount mount \
  --profile PROFILE_ID \
  --mode dynamic \
  --path "$HOME/agent-skills"
```

Mount runs in the foreground. Use another terminal for status, refresh, or unmount. Concurrent mounts need separate `--cache` directories; pass the corresponding cache to control commands too.

## Connect the Agent project

From the Skiva repository, link a verified mount into a target project:

```bash
python3 scripts/agent-link.py \
  --source-mount-path /srv/agent-skills \
  --project /workspace/my-project \
  --agent codex
```

| Agent argument | Project search directory |
| --- | --- |
| codex | .agents/skills |
| claude | .claude/skills |
| opencode | .opencode/skills |

The script refuses to overwrite existing paths and does not change global Agent configuration. If a sandbox rejects symlinks, mount directly in an allowed search directory or use an administrator-managed read-only bind mount.

## Control commands

```bash
skills-mount status
skills-mount refresh
# Rebind pinned content only between tasks
skills-mount refresh --repin
skills-mount unmount --path "$HOME/agent-skills"
```

If the Profile specifies pinnedSnapshotId, update that server binding before repin can select another authorized target.

## Offline access and revocation

- deny_on_disconnect rejects reads after the authorization lease expires; use for sensitive content.
- allow_cached permits verified cached content while offline. Uncached files remain unavailable.
- Online detection of revocation stops authorized reads. Immediate detection during a network outage is impossible.

The cache does not prefetch every file. If offline use is required, actually read necessary files beforehand and test disconnection behavior.

## Filesystem updates are not context updates

Dynamic mode preserves old handles while new opens use the refreshed index; pinned mode fixes a task snapshot. Agents may keep their own Skill indexes or prompt caches and require a reload or new session.

Host discovery was tested for Codex, Claude Code, and OpenCode. A real Pydantic AI + MiniMax model also completed the release workflow through Docker Linux FUSE. Other sandboxes and context-cache policies need separate qualification.

## Run the local Pydantic AI example

`examples/pydantic-agent/run.sh` starts an isolated backend on 8083 and its own database. Prepare Docker Desktop, uv, and model environment variables, then run:

```bash
./examples/pydantic-agent/run.sh
```

The example evaluates a simulated 150-unit reimbursement. Version 1 caps reimbursement at 100 and rejects it. After publishing version 2 with a cap of 200, dynamic approves while pinned still rejects. Rollback restores the rejection; revoked credentials prevent both mounts from reading. Each model turn rereads SKILL.md through the mount.

See the [complete setup](https://github.com/LingHeChen/skiva/tree/main/examples/pydantic-agent). Results and local OpenTelemetry traces live in .data/agent-pilot/; hosted tracing is not required.

title: Python SDK quickstart
description: Install the SDK, discover versioned Skills, and load their contents.
body:
## Installation and prerequisites

Requires Python 3.11+. Current implementation: 0.1.0; package: `skiva-sdk`; import: `skiva_sdk`. Not yet published to PyPI. These commands require Git and pin a verified commit; replace the commit explicitly when upgrading. On Windows activate with `.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1`.

```bash
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install "skiva-sdk @ git+https://github.com/LingHeChen/skiva-python.git@011bf4fbec56f453d2c4064bea9b4785ec8fc08c"
# Pydantic AI adapter (2.59.0)
python -m pip install "skiva-sdk[pydantic-ai] @ git+https://github.com/LingHeChen/skiva-python.git@011bf4fbec56f453d2c4064bea9b4785ec8fc08c"
```

Use a **client credential assigned to an enabled Agent Profile**, not an admin/API session token. Use the server origin (or reverse-proxy prefix), without `/distribution/v1`. Use HTTPS outside a trusted local environment.

```bash
export SKIVA_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:8080
export SKIVA_CLIENT_TOKEN=your-client-credential
```

The profile must have a published snapshot and authorized Skills. SDK dynamic mode respects server-side profile pins; it does not bypass them.

Create a Profile and client identity in [Clients and Agents](/docs/clients). The SDK talks directly to the distribution API; FUSE is not required.

## Discovery and loading

```python
import asyncio
from skiva_sdk import SkivaClient

async def main():
    async with SkivaClient.from_env() as client:
        async with client.bind(task_id="review-42") as skills:
            catalog = await skills.catalog()
            print(catalog.render())
            if catalog.skills:
                content = await skills.load_skill(
                    catalog.skills[0].name,
                    expected_snapshot_id=catalog.ref.snapshot_id,
                    expected_catalog_digest=catalog.catalog_digest,
                )
                print(content.render())

asyncio.run(main())
```

`Catalog` contains a `SnapshotRef`, immutable Skill metadata and `catalog_digest`. `SkillContent` contains the actual ref, catalog digest, manifest-relative path, file digest and text. Rendered envelopes escape XML markup. Names/descriptions still originate from published Skills: treat publishers as a trust boundary, not as trusted system-policy authors simply because text is escaped.

The discovery prompt tells the model to compare snapshot IDs for equality, not chronological order, and to reload content whose version differs. Rollback is handled the same way as forward updates. `catalog_digest` also changes when the authorized file set changes within one snapshot. This is a model-facing fallback, **not a guarantee that old instructions are forgotten**.

Calling `catalog.render()` only produces text. Your host application must place it in model requests; the [Pydantic AI adapter](/docs/sdk-pydantic-ai) automates that integration.

## Continue reading

[Snapshots and update policies](/docs/sdk-consistency) · [Pydantic AI integration](/docs/sdk-pydantic-ai) · [File export and framework integration](/docs/sdk-files) · [SDK reference and testing](/docs/sdk-reference)

[GitHub · skiva-python](https://github.com/LingHeChen/skiva-python)

title: Snapshots and update policies
description: Choose pinned or dynamic views and handle updates, rollback, and version conflicts.
body:
## Fixed and dynamic policies

```python
async with client.bind(consistency="dynamic") as skills:
    await skills.refresh()  # explicit reconciliation; raises on failure
    async with skills.snapshot() as batch:
        body = await batch.read_text("review/SKILL.md")
        rules = await batch.read_text("review/references/rules.md")
        original_ref = batch.ref
```

- Default `pinned`: one snapshot and filtered manifest for the binding. Future channel changes do not change it.
- Opt-in `dynamic`: reads/discovery reconcile on access after `refresh_interval` (default 5 seconds). `refresh()` forces reconciliation. No background daemon or SSE subscription.
- An expected-version load forces dynamic reconciliation even before the interval expires. Snapshot or catalog mismatch raises `VersionMismatch`; no silent substitution.
- A fully verified candidate replaces the active view atomically. Each operation captures one view; different operations can span versions. `snapshot()` captures one view for related operations, even while the enclosing dynamic session updates.
- Refresh failure aborts that operation and populates `last_refresh_error`; it never silently reports stale discovery as fresh. Later successful refresh clears the error. `transition_count` counts successful view changes.
- The client default can be overridden per binding. An explicit `source=SnapshotRef` requires pinned mode. Reuse a ref for an explicit retry, subject to current server grants/permissions.
- `view.ref` in dynamic mode is a point-in-time observation. Use returned `SkillContent.ref` or `batch.ref` for provenance.

Task/attempt IDs are optional correlation fields and auto-generated if absent. Duplicate active IDs are rejected **within one client**. There is no durable attempt store, crash resume or cross-process exactly-once guarantee in v0.1. Persist refs in your application's own storage for explicit pinned retries. A ref does not grant access and cannot bypass a new credential's permissions.

## Handle version changes

After `VersionMismatch`, obtain a fresh catalog and let the model select a Skill against it. Do not reuse old content or blindly retry business actions with side effects. Pinned views still revalidate permissions online; pinning does not grant permanent access.

Neither the SDK nor FUSE can retract content already in model history. Version labels are a fallback hint; strict cleanup requires the host to start a new task or rebuild context.

title: Pydantic AI integration
description: Refresh discovery before each model request and load Skills through version-checked tools.
body:
Complete [installation and credentials](/docs/sdk-python) with the `pydantic-ai` extra. The example reads the model identifier from `SKIVA_MODEL`; configure the provider dependencies and API credentials in your host application. This extra does not install every provider. The adapter is tested against Pydantic AI 2.59.0.

## Attach the adapter

```python
import asyncio
import os
from pydantic_ai import Agent
from pydantic_ai.capabilities import Caching
from skiva_sdk import SkivaClient, SkillSession
from skiva_sdk.integrations.pydantic_ai import SkivaSkills

async def main():
    agent = Agent(
        os.environ["SKIVA_MODEL"],
        name="skiva-agent",
        deps_type=SkillSession,
        capabilities=[Caching(), SkivaSkills()],
    )
    async with SkivaClient.from_env() as client, agent:
        async with client.bind(consistency="dynamic") as skills:
            result = await agent.run("Review this change", deps=skills)
            print(result.output)

asyncio.run(main())
```

`SkivaSkills` provides a named, dynamic discovery instruction part with **rewrite** semantics, evaluated before **every model request**. It explicitly refreshes the session at each request, bypassing the normal polling interval. It also registers `load_skill` and `read_skill_file`, requiring both expected version fields. Version mismatch/not-found become structured tool results; authorization/network failures abort rather than encourage stale fallback. It does not rewrite historical tool returns or erase derived conclusions. Provider wire placement of instructions depends on Pydantic AI and the provider.

Keep business dependencies with `SkivaSkills(get_session=lambda deps: deps.skills)`. Each run must receive its own session; the capability has no mutable run state. Attach one SkivaSkills capability per Agent (tool names are fixed). This is a dedicated discovery/tool integration, **not** a replacement for the native Harness `Skills` workspace backend. Shell/direct filesystem access is not intercepted. Configure application tracing in the host application; the SDK exports no prompts/tokens to an external telemetry service.

An active binding owns both discovery and reads. A pinned binding intentionally advertises its pinned catalog; select dynamic to follow updates within a run. Instructions are not modified while a model request is in flight. Header changes can affect prompt caching.

title: File export and framework integration
description: Export private directories and understand FUSE, Agno, and LangChain integration boundaries.
body:
## When real files are needed

```python
async with skills.snapshot() as batch:
    async with batch.materialize() as directory:
        # Give this path to a framework or awaited subprocess.
        # The child process must finish before leaving this block.
        print(directory)
```

This exports a complete private copy into a temporary directory, preserving read/execute modes. It does not create a FUSE mount or writable hardlinks to shared objects. It rejects paths incompatible with supported platforms, including case-folding collisions. Cleanup occurs on exit. File modes are not sandbox isolation against the owning process. **Direct reads of exported files bypass SDK authorization; revocation cannot recall exported bytes.** New snapshots require new exports, never rewriting an old directory.

## Choose an integration

| Scenario | Integration | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| You control model requests and tools | SDK catalog and loading APIs | Host injects discovery; Pydantic AI has a built-in adapter |
| Framework requires a directory | `snapshot().materialize()` | Fixed private copy, cleaned on exit; new versions need new directories |
| Agent only accepts a Skill search path | Linux FUSE | File updates do not automatically replace the model's Skill list |

## Agno and LangChain

There are no built-in Agno or LangChain adapters yet. If the framework accepts a local directory, pass the exported path and complete the entire task inside its context; this alone does not guarantee the framework refreshes its Skill index. Updating discovery during a run requires refreshing and injecting catalog text in the framework's model-request hook, plus wrapping the version-checked loading tools. Pydantic AI test results do not certify other frameworks.

title: SDK reference and testing
description: Understand APIs, authorization, errors, resource limits, and automated test coverage.
body:
## Validation, authorization and limits

Every snapshot is fully downloaded and validated before publication: Go-compatible manifest canonicalization, SHA-256, sizes, paths and modes. Cache is in memory and private to each view/client; no shared disk/offline cache. Default limits: 10,000 files, 8 MiB per file/manifest, 64 MiB per snapshot, 256 KiB per SKILL.md parsing input. Concurrent/retained views multiply memory use; applications should limit concurrency and release references.

Every public read/catalog/export rechecks the explicit snapshot manifest online, even for cached bytes. Changed permissions invalidate a captured view; explicit credential revocation is sticky for that client instance. Network failure blocks the operation. No offline mode, transparent network retries, or model-task retries. An authorization race after the final check and previously delivered content cannot be undone. HTTP redirects are not followed; bearer tokens are not included in SDK error messages. Raw transport instrumentation can still expose credentials; configure logging accordingly. Environment proxy/CA settings are ignored by default (`trust_env=False`); opt in explicitly with `trust_env=True` if needed, and install `httpx[socks]` for SOCKS proxies. A custom HTTPX transport can supply application TLS/proxy settings.

Useful errors: `VersionMismatch`, `ManifestChanged`, `AuthorizationDenied`, `IntegrityError`, `ProtocolError`, `LimitExceeded`, `SkillNotFound`, `TransportError`, `ClosedError`.

## Development and verification

```bash
uv sync --extra dev --extra pydantic-ai
uv run pytest -q
uv run ruff check src tests examples
uv run python -m build
uv run python examples/offline_demo.py
```

Tests use a controlled distribution fixture and Pydantic's actual `FunctionModel` agent loop, without external model calls. They cover updates/rollback, same-snapshot permission changes, concurrent reads/runs, old-content provenance, corruption, export isolation, and Go-generated manifest fixtures. The offline demo requires no server or credentials. It is not a substitute for deployment acceptance against your Skiva server and selected model provider.

See [examples/](https://github.com/LingHeChen/skiva-python/tree/main/examples/) and [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/LingHeChen/skiva-python/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). Official integration references: [Pydantic capabilities](https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/custom/), [Agent Skills implementation guide](https://agentskills.io/client-implementation/adding-skills-support).

Detailed scenarios and recorded results: [Testing guide](https://github.com/LingHeChen/skiva-python/blob/main/docs/TESTING.md).

## Verification scope

Three complex Skills (expense-audit, release-review, data-contract) cover two releases, nested references, scripts, Unicode, binary and empty files, plus concurrent updates, rollback, revocation, corruption and multi-turn model loading.

Linux CI for verified commit `011bf4f` passed 102 tests, package builds and the offline example on Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13. Agent tests use the actual Pydantic AI loop with scripted FunctionModel responses, not a live model; actual backend, provider and deployment acceptance is still required.

title: Permissions and credentials
description: Separate human sessions, repository access, and workload authorization.
body:
## Roles

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| org_admin | Organization, members, and policies |
| repo_maintainer | Repository maintenance, sync, and build diagnostics |
| release_manager | Snapshot creation, channel promotion and rollback |
| agent_manager | Profiles and client credentials |
| auditor | Audit records |

A member may have multiple roles. Authorization is checked by the server; button visibility is not an access-control boundary.

## Separate identities

Console sessions authorize human actions. Source Git credentials fetch repositories. Client tokens read Profile-authorized content. Do not interchange them.

Inject source credentials through protected environment variables or deployment Secrets. The console stores references. Do not embed credentials in repository URLs. Webhooks use separate Secret references.

## Client tokens

Registration and rotation return plaintext only once; the database stores hashes. If a response is lost, idempotent replay will not reveal the token: rotate and reconfigure the client. Credentials expire, so monitor and schedule rotation.

Revoked clients cannot renew authorization. Offline reads follow the Profile policy; offline cached availability and instantaneous offline revocation cannot both be guaranteed.

## Production sign-in

Production uses OIDC and rejects local passwords. Administrators pre-create members and assign roles. Verified enterprise email binds identities on first sign-in. Configure MFA in your enterprise IdP.

## Audit and release confirmation

Search the [audit log](/audit) by actor, action, target, and time. Sensitive updates record before/after state; promotion and rollback record reasons and channel changes.

Channel updates use concurrency control. Refresh and review again after a conflict. Do not bypass release transactions or audit records with direct database edits.

title: Deployment and troubleshooting
description: Start locally, prepare a deployment, and recover data safely.
body:
## Docker Compose

For a container-only local evaluation, run these commands from the repository root:

```bash
./scripts/setup-compose.sh
docker compose up --build -d --wait
```

Open http://localhost:3000 and sign in as admin@localhost using the password generated in .env. This starts PostgreSQL, applies migrations, and waits for application health. Data persists in named volumes. The local HTTP template uses external Git sources; hosted Git and production HTTPS/OIDC use deployments/preproduction/. See [Compose operations](https://github.com/LingHeChen/skiva/blob/main/deployments/COMPOSE.md) for ports, upgrades, and data retention.

## Start locally

Prepare Docker, Node.js 24, Git, Python 3, and Go with automatic toolchain support. The Makefile selects Go 1.26.10. From the repository root:

```bash
cp .env.example .env.local
# Set a unique administrator password of at least 14 characters
chmod 600 .env.local
make deps
make dev
```

Default ports: console 3000, API 8080, PostgreSQL 55432. To change the console port, set both SKIVA_WEB_PORT and SKIVA_WEB_ORIGIN.

## Production deployment

Configure TLS, persistent PostgreSQL and content storage, OIDC, Git host allowlists, Secret references, and backups. Migrate before starting API / workers. Templates are in deployments/compose.yaml and deployments/docker/.

Route /distribution/ directly to Go. Expose /metrics only on the monitoring network. The server image and migration command were verified locally; see deployments/preproduction/ for a single-host template. Actual domain TLS, enterprise IdP, and alert delivery still need deployment acceptance.

Detailed installation, OIDC, SSH, and restore procedures are in docs/OPERATIONS.md.

## Backup and recovery

Back up PostgreSQL together with Git / CAS data. Stop API / worker writes first for a consistent recovery point. Store backups in protected storage outside the data directory.

```bash
# Configure database, data directory, and backup location first
export SKIVA_BACKUP_DIR=/secure-backups/skiva
./scripts/backup.sh
```

Restore into an empty database and data directory. Verify backup checksums and referenced objects before switching service. Never run migration rollback tests against production.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Git connection fails | URL/ref → allowlist/DNS → Secret reference → CA or SSH known_hosts |
| No new version after sync | Diagnostics → commit → actual content changes → scan directory |
| Build succeeds but client stays old | Snapshot created → correct channel promoted → Profile → dynamic/pinned |
| A Skill disappears | Present in snapshot → authorized by Profile |
| Blob returns 403 | Client identity → Profile → snapshot authorization → file membership |
| Blob returns 503 | Missing/corrupt object; run integrity checks |
| Release returns 409 | Concurrent generation change; refresh and review |
| Files update but Agent does not | Agent index/context cache, existing handles, pinned mode |
| Lost token | Rotate credentials and sign in again |

## Verification and maintenance

```bash
make test-db
make lint test build
# Configure SKIVA_DATABASE_URL and SKIVA_DATA_DIR before inspection
make verify-artifacts
```

Keep test and application databases separate. See docs/OPERATIONS.md for maintenance and docs/ACCEPTANCE.md for evidence and boundaries. Production SLOs, enterprise identity, and real network recovery require deployment-specific acceptance.
